results.content:
The 25% auto tariff could pose a major threat to automobile titans like Hyundai and Kia that have production plants in the state, said Jennifer Safavian, president and CEO of the trade group Autos Drive America.

Safavian said her group recently conducted a study that indicates a 25% tariff on top of the 10% global levy would prompt a “sharp decline” in U.S. auto production and an average $4,000 increase in the price of new vehicles. [...] Remaining in effect, thus far, are a 25% tariff on imported cars and car parts and a 125% tariff on all Chinese goods — both of which, observers say, could deal an immediate blow to Georgia industries.
